column3: “Complete” is rendered “wholly devoted,” and “his ancestor” as “his father.”
“The matter of Uriah” is rendered “the case of Uriah.”
Close to the Hebrew; the Hebrew names Rehoboam here, as NASB does.
“Abominable image” is rendered “horrid image,” and “wadi” as “brook.”
NASB follows the reading tradition (“his own dedicated things”); the written Hebrew is difficult.
“Was sick in his feet” is rendered “was diseased in his feet.”
“Any breathing thing” is rendered “any persons alive.”
